items.evidence: REPRODUCES — a 26.1 closure that FLIPS for 26.1.1. Vanilla 26.1.1's PlaceCommand uses ResourceKeyArgument.key(Registries.CONFIGURED_FEATURE) (javap offsets 25-28; datagen commands.json agrees: the feature node is minecraft:resource_key with registry minecraft:worldgen/configured_feature). The 26.1.1 port uses ArgType::ResourceOrId("minecraft:worldgen/feature") (tree_world.rs:60-64) — the wrong registry key AND an argument type that accepts an inline SNBT value (args.rs:140-141,1661-1663), which vanilla 26.1.1 rejects. So /place feature {...} parses in Rust and fails in vanilla, and feature suggestions come from the wrong registry.

items.evidence: REPRODUCES (both parts). Vanilla 26.1.1 still has the OLD selector parser — the option-state refactor (InvertableSetOptionState, SetOnceOptionState) that closed this defect for 26.2 had NOT happened yet in 26.1.1 (neither class exists in the 26.1.1 server-game jar); the Rust parser (selector.rs) implements the 26.2 option-state shape. (a) Duplicate options: vanilla 26.1.1's EntitySelectorOptions.get() (net.minecraft.commands.arguments.selector.options.EntitySelectorOptions) runs the canUse gate BEFORE the value is read but does NOT roll back (only the unknown-option branch does setCursor(start)); the inapplicable branch throws at the cursor as it stands, i.e. at the END of the option name. Rust rolls back to the option-name START (selector.rs:331-341). For @e[type=pig,type=cow] the cursors differ by the option-name length (4 for type). (b) @a[type=player]: vanilla 26.1.1's type canUse is !parser.isTypeLimited() (lambda$bootStrap$42), and @a/@p/@r call limitToType(EntityType.PLAYER) during parseSelector, so vanilla 26.1.1 REJECTS it; Rust pushes minecraft:player into s.types without marking type_option (selector.rs:218-242), so can_use("type") stays true and Rust ACCEPTS it.
items.title: Selector option errors (1.21.7) — reproduces: vanilla 26.1.1 predates the selector refactor the Rust parser implements

items.evidence: CLOSED (with the 26.1 run's correction to the 26.2 record). Real vanilla 26.1.1 DOES suggest recipes: CommandSourceStack.suggestRegistryElements has a Registries.RECIPE special case (javap offsets 0-36) suggesting from RecipeManager.getRecipes(), even though there is no minecraft:recipe registry. For the case in the corpus (recipe give @s minecraft:stick), the two suggestion lists agree by static comparison: real vanilla suggests minecraft:stick, minecraft:stick_from_bamboo_item, minecraft:sticky_piston — exactly what Rust suggests from its learnable_recipes list (args.rs:1722-1723, 1,491 entries). Note for the run: it WILL show recipe suggestion mismatches, but they are an ORACLE artifact: the oracle's Src class overrides suggestRegistryElements (VanillaCommandParseOracle.java:93-99) to look the registry up in the RegistryAccess and return Suggestions.empty() when absent, bypassing vanilla's RECIPE special case. The residual real divergence (special recipes Rust omits) is recorded as B9-G17.
items.title: Suggestions for complete arguments (1.21.7: recipe) — closed: real vanilla 26.1.1 suggests recipes, matching Rust; the run's mismatches are an oracle artifact

items.evidence: REPRODUCES — a 26.1 closure that FLIPS for 26.1.1. Vanilla 26.1.1's /item and /execute if items use minecraft:item_slot (single) and minecraft:item_slots (multi) — SlotArgument, read-until-space (lambda$parse$0: c != ' '), slot.unknown / slot.only_single_allowed at the cursor after the word, and the slot_ranges() table matches vanilla 26.1.1's SlotRanges entry for entry. The 26.1 port had removed the 26.3-only SlotSource argument type and used ArgType::Slot / ArgType::Slots. The 26.1.1 port uses ArgType::SlotSource everywhere in /item (tree_misc.rs:171,189,203) and in execute if|unless items|slots (tree_execute.rs:239): a slot range name, else a slot-source id or inline value (args.rs:1647-1660, resource_or_id on minecraft:slot_source — a registry that does not exist in 26.1.1). So a non-range word is accepted by Rust as a slot-source id/inline value where vanilla errors slot.unknown, and the single-vs-multi distinction (slot.only_single_allowed) is lost. Node names differ too (B9-G16: slots vs slot, sourceSlots vs sourceSlot).
items.title: Slot errors (1.21.7) — reproduces: SlotSource is back in the tree; vanilla 26.1.1 uses item_slot/item_slots

items.evidence: REPRODUCES for 26.1.1 (same shape as 26.1, count 24 not 23). items.evidence: NEW for 26.1.1 (the 26.1 port had none of these). The Rust tree registers three subcommands vanilla 26.1.1 never had. /item fill and /item override: tree_misc.rs:181 builds for mode in ["replace", "fill", "override"]; vanilla 26.1.1's /item node has only modify and replace (datagen commands.json). /execute if slots and /execute unless slots: tree_execute.rs:226 builds for kind in ["items", "slots"] inside conditionals, which is shared by if and unless (tree_execute.rs:89); vanilla 26.1.1's /execute if and /execute unless nodes have items but no slots. All three parse in Rust and fail as unknown subcommands in vanilla. 26.3-form carry-overs in the re-ported tree — the same systemic cause as G02's three extra top-level commands, recorded separately because they are subcommand-level and G02 is the top-level diff. Minor: gamemaster-only, no vanilla equivalent to confuse players with.

systemic_note: The 26.1.1 port re-ported command code from the 26.3 form instead of carrying the 26.1 tree's adaptations: five 26.1 closures flip back to gaps (G03 /place feature as ResourceOrId, G05 /publish without gamemode, G07b multi-entity item source, G12 SlotSource back in the tree, G13 the 62-entry 26.3 argument-type table), G02 widens from one extra top-level command to three (posteffect, unpublish, compute), and a new item (G18) records three 26.3-era subcommands (/item fill, /item override, /execute if|unless slots). On top of that, the 26.1-carried defects that never got fixed still reproduce (G07a item-modifier function key, G08 particle Name compound, G09 selector option-state), and all three in-scope oracles fail with the same error counts as 26.1 (TeamColor, Hud, EntityTypes). 8 of 13 re-checked 1.21.7 defects reproduce (vs 4 of 13 for 26.1). The one genuine improvement over 26.1 is H01: the probe compiles (FrameContext keeps the 26.3 form), so the command_parse measurement ran end-to-end. The remaining risk is execution, not parsing: 18 of 22 drivers are unrun e2e drivers.
